87:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Ala The evidence for this is what Al-Bukhari narrated: Abdun told us, my father told me, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, who said: The first of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to come to us were Mus’ab ibn ‘Umair and Ibn Umm Maktum, and they began to recite the Qur’an to us. Then came ‘Ammar, Bilal, and Sa’d, then came ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab with twenty, then came the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I never saw the people of Madinah rejoice over anything as they did over him until I saw the little girls and boys saying: This is the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has come. But he did not come until I had recited Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High in a similar surah. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Thawir ibn Abi Fakhita, on the authority of his father, on the authority of ‘Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) loved this surah: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. Ahmad alone transmitted it. It was proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muadh: Why did you not pray ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ ‘By the sun and its brightness, and by the night when it covers’? Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Muntashir, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Habib bin Salim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite on the two Eids ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ and ‘Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming’? If it fell on a Friday, he would recite them both. This is how the chain of transmission of this hadith appears in Musnad al-Imam Ahmad. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, as did Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abu ‘Awanah, Jarir, and Shu’bah, all three of them from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir from his father from Habib ibn Salim from al-Nu’man ibn Bashir. al-Tirmidhi said: And al-Thawri and Mis’ar narrated it likewise from Ibrahim. He said: And Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated it from Ibrahim from his father from Habib ibn Salim from his father from al-Nu’man, and it is not known that Habib narrated from his father. Ibn Majah narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Sabah from Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah from Ibrahim ibn al-Muntashir from his father from Habib ibn Salim from al-Nu’man, as it was narrated by the group, and God knows best. The wording of Muslim and the people of Sunnah is: He used to recite on the two Eids and on Friday ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ and ‘Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?’ Sometimes they came together on the same day and he would recite them both. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, and ‘Aishah, the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite in witr: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, “Say: O you disbelievers,” “Say: He is God, the One,” and The two Mu’awwidhat, Aisha added. This is how the hadith was narrated via Jabir, Abu Umamah Siddi bin Ajlan, Abdullah bin Masoud, Imran bin Husayn, and Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with them. Were it not for the fear of making it too long, we would have included whatever chains of transmission and texts we could find for that, but this brief guidance is sufficient, and God knows best. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Imam Ahmad said: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Musa - meaning Ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi - told us, my paternal uncle Iyas ibn Amir told us, I heard Uqba ibn Amir al-Juhani say: When the verse, So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to us, Include it in your bowing. When the verse, Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, was revealed, he said, Include it in your prostration. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, from Musa ibn Ayyub, with this chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Isra’il told us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited, Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, he would say, Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Abu Dawud narrated it in this way, from Zuhayr ibn Harb, from Waki’, with this chain of transmission. He said, “Waki’ was contradicted in it. Abu Waki’ and Shu’bah narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from Sa’id, from Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ath-Thawri said, from al-Suddi, from Abd al-Khayr, who said, “I heard Ali recite, ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ and he said, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’” Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani, that when Ibn Abbas recited Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, he would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. And when he recited I swear by the Day of Resurrection, and reached the end of it, Is He not able to give life to the dead? he would say: Glory be to You, and yes. And Qatada said: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, he mentioned to us that when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, he would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. And God Almighty’s statement: Who created and proportioned means He created creation and proportioned every creature in the best of forms. And the Almighty’s saying: And He Who has determined and guided. Mujahid said: He has guided mankind to misery and happiness and He has guided livestock to their pastures. This verse is like the Almighty’s saying, informing us about Moses, who said to Pharaoh: Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and nature and then guided it. That is, He determined a measure and guided the creation to it, as is proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God determined the destinies of the creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was over the water. And the Almighty’s saying: And He Who brought forth pasture, that is, of all kinds of plants and crops, and made it black stubble. Ibn Abbas said: Changing dry stubble. And something similar was reported from Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Jarir said: Some of the scholars of Arabic speech were of the view that this is from the deferred meaning of bringing forward, and that the meaning of speech is and He who brought forth the pasture, Ahwa: green to black, then He made it stubble after that. Then Ibn Jarir said: Although this is possible, it is not correct because it contradicts the sayings of the people of interpretation. And the statement of God, the Most High, We will make you recite meaning O Muhammad and you will not forget. This is a statement from God, the Most High, and a promise from Him to him that He will make him recite a recitation that he will not forget except what God wills. This is the preferred choice of Ibn Jarir. Qatada said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, did not forget anything except what God wills. It was said that what is meant by his statement, and you will not forget is a request, and the meaning of the exception in this is what occurs from abrogation, meaning do not forget what We make you recite except what God wills. He lifted it up, so there is no harm in leaving it. And the statement of God, the Most High, Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden, meaning He knows what the servants declare openly and what they conceal of their words and deeds. Nothing of that is hidden from Him. God the Almighty says: {And We will make easy for you [the path] easy [for you]} meaning, We will make good deeds and words easy for you, and We will legislate for you an easy, tolerant, upright, and just law in which there is no crookedness, difficulty, or hardship. God the Almighty says: {Then remind, if the reminder should benefit} meaning, remind when reminding is beneficial. From here, etiquette is taken in disseminating knowledge and not disclosing it to anyone other than its people, as the Commander of the Faithful, Ali may God be pleased with him said: If you tell people something that their minds cannot comprehend, it will be a trial for some of them. He said: “Tell people what they know. Do you wish that God and His Messenger would be accused of lying?” God the Almighty says: {He who fears will be reminded} meaning, he will be admonished by what you convey, O Muhammad, from the heart, who fears God and knows that he will meet Him. “But the most wretched will avoid it * who will enter the Great Fire * and then neither die therein nor live} meaning, he will neither die and find rest nor live a life that benefits him, rather it will be harmful to him, because because of it he will feel the painful torment and various types of humiliation he will be punished with. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday narrated to us on the authority of Sulayman, meaning al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for the people of Hell, who are its people, they neither die nor live. As for the people for whom God wants mercy, He causes them to die in Hell, and the intercessors enter upon them, and a man takes his supporters and causes them to grow—or he said—grow—in the River of Life—or he said Life—or he said Animals—or he said River of Paradise—and they grow like the seed in the mud of a torrent.” He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you not see that a tree is green, then it becomes yellow, then it becomes green? He said: Some of them said: It is as if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the desert. Ahmad also said: Ismail told us, Saeed bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for the people of Hell, who are its people, they will neither die in it nor live. Rather, there will be people - or something like that - who will be afflicted by Hell because of their sins - or he said because of their transgressions - and it will cause them to die a death until they become charcoal. Then intercession will be permitted, and they will be brought in groups, and they will grow on the rivers of Paradise. It will be said: O people of Paradise, pour water over them. So they will grow like a seed in the muck of a torrent.” He said: A man from the people then said: It is as if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the desert. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal and Shu’bah, both of them on the authority of Abu Salamah Saeed bin Yazid, with a similar chain of narration. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Iyas Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The people of Hell whom God does not want to bring out will neither die in it nor live. The people of Hell whom God wants to bring out will cause them to die in it.” Death until they become charcoal, then they emerge as flocks and are thrown upon the rivers of Paradise, and water from the rivers of Paradise is sprinkled upon them, and they grow as a seed grows in the silt of a torrent. And God Almighty said, informing us about the people of Hellfire: And they will call, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!’ He will say, ‘Indeed, you will remain.’ And God Almighty said: They will not be put to death so that they die, nor will their punishment be lightened for them, and other verses with this meaning.

87:14: God the Almighty says: Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself meaning, purifies himself from bad morals and follows what God has revealed to the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And remembers the name of his Lord and prays meaning, establishes the prayer at its appointed times, seeking God’s pleasure, obeying God’s command, and complying with God’s law. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibad ibn Ahmad al-Azrami told us, my uncle Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself He said: Whoever bears witness that there is no god but God, and removes all rivals to Him, and bears witness that I am the Messenger of God “And remembers the name of his Lord and prays” He said: It refers to the five daily prayers, maintaining them, and paying attention to them. Then he said: It is not narrated from Jabir except from this source. Ibn Abbas also said: What is meant by this are the five daily prayers, and Ibn Jarir chose this view. Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Amli told me, Marwan ibn Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Khalda, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Aaliyah, and he said to me: When you go out tomorrow to the Eid, pass by me. He said: So I passed by him, and he said: Have you eaten anything? I said: Yes. He said: Did you pour water over yourself? I said: Yes. He said: Then tell me, what did you do with your zakat? I said: I have directed it. He said: I only wanted you for this. Then he recited: Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. And he said: The people of Medina do not see any charity better than this or providing water to drink. I said: We have narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, that he used to order the people to give Zakat al-Fitr and recite this verse: Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Abu al-Ahwas said: If a beggar comes to one of you while he wants to pray, let him put it forward before his prayer, for God the Most High says: Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Qatadah said about this verse: Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays, he purifies his wealth and pleases his Creator. Then God Almighty said: Rather, you prefer the life of this world meaning you give it precedence over the matters of the Hereafter and prefer it over what is beneficial and better for you in your life and your afterlife. And the Hereafter is better and more lasting meaning God’s reward in the Hereafter is better and more lasting than this world, for this world is lowly and fleeting, while the Hereafter is noble and everlasting. So how can a rational person prefer what will perish over what will last and be concerned with what will soon pass away and neglect concern for the eternal and everlasting home? Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Dhuwaid told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This world is the home of those who have no home, and the wealth of those who have no wealth, and it is gathered for those who have no mind. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Yahya ibn Wadh told us, Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Urfajah al-Thaqafi, who said: I recited to Ibn Mas’ud, Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, Who created and proportioned, Who determined and guided, Who brought forth pasture, Then made it dark stubble up to His saying, But you prefer the life of this world. He stopped reciting and turned to his companions and said: We prefer this world over the Hereafter. The people were silent, so he said: We prefer this world because we have seen its adornments, its women, its food and its drink, and the Hereafter has been turned away from us, so we have chosen this immediate life and left the delayed one. This from him is in the form of humility and condescension, or it is describing the genus as it is, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi told us, Ismail ibn Ja`far told us, `Amr ibn Abi `Amr told me, on the authority of al-Muttalib ibn `Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash`ari, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever loves his worldly life will harm his Hereafter, and whoever loves his Hereafter will harm his worldly life, so prefer what remains over what perishes. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. He also narrated it on the authority of Abu Salamah al-Khuza`i, on the authority of al-Darawardi, on the authority of `Amr ibn Abi `Amr, with a similar chain of transmission. And the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses, al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Nasr ibn `Ali told us, Mu`tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: When the verse, Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses, was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of this—or this was—was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
